2027-03-09.title: Fifth Tuesday of the Great Fast
2027-03-09.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-03-09.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). The Latin Church commemorates St Frances of Rome today.
theo: Paul is collecting money. For years he gathered a collection from the Gentile churches of Greece and Asia for the poor believers in Jerusalem, and in this chapter he encourages the Corinthians to finish what they had promised. He does not scold; he speaks of God as a farmer who supplies the farmer: “He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.” Giving is sowing, and God is the one who makes it grow. “You will be enriched in every way for your great generosity, which will produce thanksgiving to God through us.” What is remarkable is where Paul's eyes rest. The collection will feed the hungry, but it will do more: it will make the poor of Jerusalem give thanks to God, and pray for the Gentiles who once seemed strangers. The gift builds the one Church: “they long for you and pray for you because of the surpassing grace of God that he has given you.” And then, as if all talk of money had brought him to the greatest Gift of all, Paul breaks into praise: “Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift!” The Great Fast has always had three companions: prayer, fasting and almsgiving. Almsgiving here is not a tax paid to God, but seed sown in his field, which returns as thanksgiving and communion.

The Gospel takes us to the road from Jerusalem down to Jericho, a steep and lonely road where robbers waited. A man lies there half dead. A priest and a Levite pass by on the other side. “But a Samaritan while traveling came near him; and when he saw him, he was moved with pity.” Jesus' hearers did not expect the hero to be a Samaritan, a member of a people with whom they had long quarrelled. Everything the Samaritan does is concrete: “He went to him and bandaged his wounds, having poured oil and wine on them. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.” He pays two denarii, about two days' wages, and promises more. The lawyer had asked, “who is my neighbor?”, a question about where to draw the line. Jesus turns it round: “Which of these three, do you think, was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of the robbers?” “The one who showed him mercy.” “Go and do likewise.” The Fathers saw Christ himself in the Samaritan, who came down to our road, poured the oil and wine of the sacraments on our wounds, and brought us to the inn of the Church. The Latin Church today remembers St Frances of Rome, a noblewoman, wife and mother who, through famine and plague, turned her family's house into a storehouse and hospital for the poor of Rome. She did not leave her home or her marriage to be a neighbour; she opened them.
outline: Ask: whose wounds have I passed by on the other side?
Almsgiving as sowing in God's field.
live: Visit, call or help one person this week whom you have been passing by: a lonely neighbour, a sick relative, a migrant worker.
Decide on a definite Lenten alms and give it before Hosanna Sunday.
2027-03-09.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you came down to our road, saw us half dead, and were moved with pity. You poured oil and wine on our wounds and brought us to the inn of your Church. Make us neighbours to everyone we meet; open our hands to sow generously, and our lips to give thanks for your indescribable gift. Through the prayers of St Frances of Rome, make our homes places of mercy. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Good Samaritan still comes near: he pours the oil and wine of his grace on our wounds, and gives himself, the indescribable gift, for which we give thanks.

quick: Paul: God gives seed to the sower; generous giving produces thanksgiving and communion.
The Samaritan did not ask who his neighbour was; he came near and showed mercy.
2027-03-09.action: Come near this week to one person you have been passing by.
2027-03-09.question: Whom have I passed by on the other side?

family.explain: A man was hurt by robbers and left on the road. Two important people saw him and walked past. Then a man from Samaria, a stranger, stopped. He cleaned the man's wounds, put him on his donkey, and paid for him to be looked after. Jesus says: be like him. A neighbour is anyone who needs our help.
family.intention: We pray for those who are hurt, alone or forgotten, and for all who help them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who needs our help this week, and what can we do for them together?”

illus: On the national highway near Angamaly a motorcyclist lay on the road after an accident one evening. Cars slowed down; several people took videos on their phones; no one stopped. A migrant worker from Odisha, going home from a construction site, put down his bag, turned the injured man on his side as he had seen done, stopped an autorickshaw and went with him to the hospital, paying the fare from his day's wages. When the young man's family came, they wanted to thank him, but he had already gone back to his room. The parish priest told the story at the Lenten retreat that week, and simply read the Gospel after it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Samaritan of our souls, come near to us as we pray, and teach us to come near to others. Amen.
share: He who supplies seed to the sower (2 Corinthians 9:10). Do I give as one who sows, trusting God for the harvest?
When he saw him, he was moved with pity (Luke 10:33). When did I last let someone's suffering move me to act?
Go and do likewise (Luke 10:37). Who is the person on my road this week?
interc: For the Church, that she may be an inn where every wounded person is cared for.
For victims of accidents and violence, and for those who stop to help them.
For migrant workers in our land, that they may be treated as neighbours.
For families, through the prayers of St Frances of Rome, that their homes may be open to the poor.
For our group, that we may not pass by on the other side.
pm.close: Father of mercies, your Son came down our road and bound up our wounds. Fill us with his compassion, make us generous sowers of good, and let our lives become thanksgiving for your indescribable gift. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the Corinthians that God supplies seed to the sower and bread for food, and will multiply the harvest of our righteousness (2 Corinthians 9:10). When we give alms in this Great Fast, we are not paying God a tax. We are sowing in his field.

And the harvest is more than bread for the hungry: it is thanksgiving to God, and prayer and love between people who were strangers. That is why Paul ends with a cry of praise: thanks be to God for his indescribable gift! (2 Corinthians 9:15).

In the Gospel a priest and a Levite pass by a wounded man. But a Samaritan, a stranger, sees him and is moved with pity. He bandages his wounds, pours oil and wine, carries him to an inn and pays for his care (Luke 10:33–35).

Jesus says to us: go and do likewise (Luke 10:37). St Frances of Rome opened her house to the poor during famine and plague. This week, let us come near to one person we have been passing by. That is how the fast becomes mercy. Amen.
kids: Children, a man was hurt and lying on the road. Two people walked past, but a kind stranger stopped and helped him. Jesus says: be like that kind man. Who can you help this week, even in a small way?

intro: God who gives seed to the sower, the Samaritan who was moved with pity, and the indescribable gift that turns all our giving into thanksgiving.

q: Since there will never cease to be some in need on the earth, I therefore command you, “Open your hand to the poor and needy neighbor in your land.”
He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
points.apply: Fix a definite Lenten alms today and give it before Hosanna Sunday.

sub: The priest and the Levite passed by.
Oil, wine, an inn and two denarii.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
But a Samaritan while traveling came near him; and when he saw him, he was moved with pity.
points.apply: Come near this week to one person you have been passing by.

q: What shall I return to the LORD for all his bounty to me?
Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift!
points.apply: Before Communion at your next Qurbana, thank Christ by name for one wound he has healed in you.

concl: Almsgiving is sowing in God's field, and its harvest is thanksgiving and communion.
Christ came near to us on our road; let us go and do likewise.
2027-03-09.resolve: Choose one person you have been passing by, and come near to them before Sunday.
